Tryambakeśvara
(‘the Lord with three eyes’)
------------------------------------------
This is a well-known place of पिल्ग्रिमगे in the Maharashtra State. It is 29 kms. (18 miles) from the city of नासिक्. (See NĀSIK also.) It is here that the गोदावरी river takes its birth (in the Brahmagiri hills). The temple of Lord शिव known as त्र्यम्बकेश्वर is situated in the midst of three mountains—Brahma-giri, Nīlagiri and Kālagiri.
The temple is fairly big. The garbha-gṛha (sanctum) contains three liṅgas representing ब्रह्मा, विष्णु and शिव. They are among the twelve ज्योतिर्लिङ्गस् (See JYOTIRLIṄGAS.). There is also a puṣkariṇī (temple tank) called अमृत-varṣiṇī, the water of which is used to bathe the liṅgas.
The present temple structure is said to have been built by Bājī Rao Peṣvā in A.

.
A big tank, 28 metres by 25 metres (94 feet by 85 feet), known as Kuśāvarta situated at a short distance from the temple is considered very sacred.
The place abounds in tīrthas (holy tanks) like Bilvatīrtha, Viśvanāthatīrtha and Mukundatīrtha. There are also several temples and shrines dedicated to गङ्गा-देवी, Jaleśvara, केदारनाथ, Rāmeśvara, Gautameśvara, राम, कृष्ण, परशुराम, Lakṣmīnārāyaṇa, Māruti (Hanumān) and so on.
On the Kālagiri (also spelt as कौल-giri) there is a place containing 108 Śivaliṅgas.
Several maṭhas or monasteries and samādhis (places of बुरिअल् of great saints) also abound in this area.

Tryambakahoma
------------------------------------------
This is a minor rite forming the last part of the साकमेध sacrifice. It consists in making an offering of cakes in a palāśa leaf at the crossroad (of the village or town) with the famous मन्त्र tryambakaṁ yajāmahe (Vājasaneyī Saṁhitā 3.6) addressed to रुद्र-शिव.
See also SĀKAMEDHA.
